position.summary: The Iran war intensified during this window as Iran escalated attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, sinking at least two cargo ships and a container ship, while the US military considered deploying the 'Mother of All Bombs' for future strikes. Oil prices surged past $100 per barrel as the US blockade kept Iranian crude exports at zero. Iran-backed Houthis struck Saudi Arabia's Aramco headquarters and the Yemeni presidential palace in Aden, prompting Riyadh to accuse Tehran of encouraging escalation, which Iran denied. In the UK, the prime minister said Iran's IRGC was likely behind a plot at RAF Fairford, and MI5 warned Iran was targeting military sites. A German court sentenced two men for plotting to kill a Jewish community leader on Iran's behalf, and a Norwegian teen received 20 years for a UK murder plot tied to an Iran-linked group. Diplomatically, Iran called the US response to a Hormuz proposal insufficient, while the Kremlin said Putin relayed Iran's peace position to Trump. The US issued fresh sanctions, and Lebanon revoked the license of Iran's Bank Saderat under US pressure. Russia reportedly delivered missiles to Tehran to reconstitute its arsenal.

key_events.event: Iran escalated attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, sinking multiple cargo ships and a container ship, driving oil prices above $100.
The US military reportedly considered using the 'Mother of All Bombs' in potential future strikes on Iran.
Iran-backed Houthis struck Saudi Aramco's headquarters and the Yemeni presidential palace in Aden; Saudi Arabia accused Iran of encouraging escalation, which Tehran denied.
UK PM said Iran's IRGC was likely behind the RAF Fairford incident, and MI5 warned Iran was stepping up targeting of British military sites.
Iran fortified its nuclear sites and braced for possible US strikes after the midterm elections, while the Pentagon raised the number of US military killed to 21.
US inflation jumped to 3.7% and European gas hit wartime highs as the Iran war drove energy prices sharply higher.
Iran called the US response to its Hormuz proposal insufficient, while the Kremlin said Putin relayed Iran's peace position to Trump.
A German court sentenced two men for plotting to kill the leader of Germany's Jewish community on behalf of Iran.
The US issued fresh Iran-related sanctions and Lebanon revoked the license of Iran's Bank Saderat under American pressure.
Russia reportedly delivered missiles to Iran to help reconstitute its arsenal during the war.

emoji_reasons: Iran's intensified attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, sinking multiple vessels, dominated the week's security news.
The US military's reported consideration of the 'Mother of All Bombs' for future strikes on Iran signaled a potential major escalation.
Oil prices topped $100 and US inflation hit 3.7% as the war's economic fallout spread globally.

naive_forecast.summary: The coming week will bring further escalation in the Iran war as both sides prepare for the US midterm elections. Iran will intensify its campaign against shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, sinking or damaging additional vessels to pressure global oil markets and demonstrate strength before November's vote. The US will weigh a major conventional strike, with Trump's specific mention of Pickaxe Mountain suggesting a decision on the Mother of All Bombs option is imminent. Oil prices will climb further as supply disruptions compound, pushing US crude above $105. Diplomatically, Iran will deliver its formal response to the US Hormuz proposal, which will be insufficient to satisfy Washington but keep a thin channel of negotiation open. The Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia will draw Iran into a public dispute with Riyadh over responsibility. Domestically, political infighting will deepen as economic pressure from the blockade takes its toll. A full Hormuz closure declaration would mark a dramatic new escalation, though it remains less probable than incremental attacks on individual vessels.

statements.text: The United States conducts a military strike on Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site using the GBU-43/B conventional bomb.
US crude oil price exceeds $105 per barrel.
Iran sinks or damages at least one additional commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran issues a formal written response to the US proposal on the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran declares the complete closure of the Strait of Hormuz to all commercial shipping.

crystal_forecast.summary: The coming week will see Iran intensify its campaign against shipping in the Strait of Hormuz as it deliberately escalates before the US midterm elections. At least one more vessel will be sunk, keeping oil prices above $100 per barrel and deepening the global energy crunch. The US will weigh whether to deploy the Massive Ordnance Air Blast weapon against Iranian targets, though Trump's public hedging suggests a strike is not yet decided. On the diplomatic track, Iran will formally respond to the US position on the Hormuz proposal, most probably with a rejection that keeps the stalemate intact. The Houthi-Saudi axis will see further strikes on Saudi infrastructure. Iran will also test its stated intent to target Starlink and Gulf digital infrastructure, potentially marking a new phase of the war in the technology domain. Economic pain will spread further as sanctions tighten and the blockade keeps Iranian crude exports at zero.
crystal_forecast.reasoning: With no prior forecast to correct against, I applied the standard caution: forecasters overestimate dramatic military events and underestimate slow economic ones. The trend is clearly toward escalation, so I gave high probability to another ship sinking. However, the MOAB strike is being considered rather than planned, and Bloomberg's analysis that it would miss buried sites suggests the US is keeping it as a bargaining chip, so I kept that probability moderate. The oil-above-$100 statement is the one most likely to be underweighted by a naive reader who focuses on dramatic headlines, so I gave it high confidence. The Starlink cyberattack is the surprise pick: Iran has stated intent but the jump from rhetoric to measurable disruption is a big step, hence the low probability.

statements.text: Iran sinks at least one more ship in the Strait of Hormuz during the week of October 16 to 23.
The United States conducts a strike on Iran using the Massive Ordnance Air Blast weapon.
US crude oil prices close above $100 per barrel on at least three trading days during the week of October 16 to 23.

Iran announces a cyberattack on Starlink terminals in the Middle East that causes measurable service degradation for regional users.

display.headline: Iran Sinks More Ships in Hormuz, Oil Holds Above $100
emoji_reasons: Iran's campaign of sinking cargo ships in the Strait of Hormuz is the central story driving everything else this week.
Oil prices staying above $100 per barrel is the biggest real-world consequence for people filling up their cars.
The US is weighing whether to drop its most powerful non-nuclear bomb on Iran, a decision that could reshape the war.
display.tldr: Iran will sink at least one more ship in the Strait of Hormuz, keeping oil above $100 per barrel. The US is considering a massive bomb strike but has not decided. Diplomacy remains stuck with Iran likely rejecting the latest US proposal.
display.eli5:
The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow stretch of water between Iran and Oman where about a fifth of the world's oil passes through every day. Iran has been sinking ships there for weeks, and it is about to keep doing so. Think of it like a toll booth where the country controlling the booth keeps ramming boats to make everyone pay more for fuel.

Why is Iran doing this? It is trying to hurt the global economy and make people angry at the US government right before American midterm elections in November. The more ships sink, the higher oil prices climb, and the more voters grumble about gas prices. It is a deliberate political move, not just random fighting.

There is about an 80 percent chance, roughly four out of five, that at least one more ship gets sunk this week. Oil will almost certainly stay above $100 per barrel for most of the week. The US military is also debating whether to drop its "Mother of All Bombs" on Iranian targets, but there is only about a one in three chance that actually happens this week. Trump is publicly hedging, which usually means the decision is not final.

The biggest surprise would be if Iran managed to disrupt Starlink internet service in the Middle East. Starlink is Elon Musk's satellite internet, and if Iran could make it glitch or go down for users in Gulf countries, that would mark a new phase of the war hitting technology instead of just ships and buildings. The odds of that are low, about one in five, but Iran has already said it wants to try.
